reader.requirement: At --std 85, a relative FD must accept the Sequential I-O BLOCK CONTAINS clause (§1985:VII.3.3) in every form its format allows: integer-2 alone or integer-1 TO integer-2, RECORDS or CHARACTERS or neither (CHARACTERS implied), with the 1985 integer rule (no zero, no sign), no ordering rule on the pair, and the same values in every BLOCK CONTAINS clause of an external connector's descriptions (GR5).

edition-consulted.switches: the integer-2 > integer-1 rule applies only from 2002 (§2023:13.18.10.3 SR1); at 85 equal and inverted bounds translate
below 2002 CheckFileDescriptions asks GR5 (BLOCK CONTAINS agreement across an external connector's FDs, COBOL6847)

IntegerOperandRules.Classify(ctx, DialectLevel): the slot's zero permission and the message's citation (§1985:III.2 at 85); BLOCK CONTAINS 0 is refused (COBOL2386), the nonzero slot as at the latest edition

reader.notes: BLOCK CONTAINS has no effect on disk storage (GR1 to GR3 are implementor or environment matters), so the observable obligations are acceptance, the integer rule and GR5, and all hold at 85. The '-2' refusal is a parse error, not a named integer-rule message.

refuter.evidence: Rendered PDF pages 397 (VII-23) and 444 (VIII-14): {RECORDS|CHARACTERS} are braces with CHARACTERS not underlined (the transcription of page 444 wrongly underlines CHARACTERS), so by §1985:IV.2.1.4 CHARACTERS is the default and the bare form is legal; blk_nocont.cob 'BLOCK 4.' compiles and runs (R 00 ABCD). Refusals: blk_plus '+2 RECORDS' and blk_plus1 '+1 TO 4' refused (parse error COBOL0001/1970); blk_dec '2.0 RECORDS' refused COBOL5506; blk_zero1 '0 TO 4' refused COBOL2386 (§1985:III.2 integer neither signed nor zero); blk_both 'RECORDS CHARACTERS' refused. ext_unit / ext_unit2: external FDs '2 TO 6 RECORDS' vs '2 TO 6 CHARACTERS' / '2 TO 6' compile, consistent with GR5 which compares only integer-1 and integer-2. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.2.1.4; OK §1985:III.2; OK §1985:VII.3.3.3 GR5.
